# The Ledger

> A free, open-source magazine and blog template for Next.js 16, built entirely
> with VivekUI. Typography-first, server-rendered, twelve sample articles across
> four desks, and charts embedded inside the article bodies.

- Live site: https://theledger.vivekkumarsingh.in
- Source: https://github.com/intellectwithvivek/theledger
- Clone: `git clone https://github.com/intellectwithvivek/theledger.git`
- Licence: MIT — free for commercial use, credit removable
- RSS: https://theledger.vivekkumarsingh.in/feed.xml

The Ledger is a demonstration site. It exists to show what a real editorial
product looks like when it is assembled from a single component library with no
Tailwind, no shadcn, no MUI and no configuration file.

## Attribution

This entire website is built with VivekUI, a free React component library with
zero runtime dependencies. 91 accessible React components and 6 SVG charts.
One install, one CSS import, no config.

- Install: `npm i @the_viveksingh/vivek-ui`
- Documentation: https://ui.vivekkumarsingh.in/docs
- Components: https://ui.vivekkumarsingh.in/docs/components
- Charts: https://ui.vivekkumarsingh.in/docs/charts
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@the_viveksingh/vivek-ui
- GitHub: https://github.com/intellectwithvivek/vivek_UI
- Author: Vivek Kumar Singh — https://vivekkumarsingh.in/

## Stack

- Next.js 16.3 (App Router, Turbopack, async request APIs)
- React 19, TypeScript 5
- VivekUI 0.5 — the only UI dependency
- Node.js 20.9+ (22 LTS recommended)
- Deployed on Vercel

## Routes

- `/` — front page: nameplate, breaking ticker, lead story, eight-card Latest
  grid, a Most read rail with per-article sparklines, four desk tabs, subscribe
  band.
- `/article/[slug]` — one of twelve articles. Reading-progress bar, breadcrumb,
  byline card, body in Prose, share row, three related cards, comments empty
  state. Two articles close with a "Quick answers" FAQ block.
- `/category/[slug]` — one of four desks (systems, culture, data, dispatches)
  with a paginated grid.
- `/built-with` — the colophon: every section of the site mapped to the VivekUI
  component that renders it, each deep-linked to its documentation page.
- `/feed.xml` — RSS 2.0 for all twelve articles.
- `/sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt`, `/manifest.webmanifest`

## Content

Twelve articles, 300–500 words each, across four desks:

- Systems — architecture, caching, CSS and the cost of maintenance.
- Culture — group chats, editing, typography and the shape of the open web.
- Data — data journalism, each piece built around real chart components.
- Dispatches — reported field notes: a data centre night shift, a letterpress
  shop in Fort Kochi, a week without algorithmic feeds.

The lead story, "The numbers behind India's developer boom", embeds a LineChart
and a BarChart directly inside its Prose body, with captions — charts living in
content, the way a real data story works.

All twelve articles are fictional and written for this template. Every figure in
them is invented for demonstration and must not be cited as fact.

## Notable technical points

- Article bodies are a typed discriminated union of blocks, not HTML strings, so
  a chart can be a real component between two paragraphs and nothing ever calls
  `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` on content.
- Charts (Sparkline, LineChart, BarChart) are pure SVG with no client boundary,
  so they render completely on the server and ship a visually hidden data table
  for assistive technology.
- Structured data: WebSite with SearchAction on the front page, NewsArticle plus
  BlogPosting per article, CollectionPage with an ItemList on every desk,
  BreadcrumbList on every nested route, and FAQPage on the two articles with a
  "Quick answers" block and on `/built-with`.
- `app/sitemap.ts` and `app/robots.ts` are generated from the content, so
  `lastModified` reflects the articles rather than the build time.
- No `!important` anywhere. VivekUI wraps every selector in `:where()`, so a
  single flat class outranks it.
- Every route is statically prerendered at build time.
